## Comparability note

GE underwent two major spin-offs during this period: GE HealthCare (completed January 3, 2023) and GE Vernova (completed April 2, 2024). As a result, the "as originally reported" FY2022 total revenue for General Electric Company ($76,555 million, including HealthCare and Vernova) [DOC ge_fy2022_10k.txt] is **not** comparable to today's GE Aerospace entity, since that figure included businesses no longer part of the company.

The FY2024 10-K, filed by the entity now named GE Aerospace, recasts prior-period results to reflect only continuing operations (i.e., excluding both GE HealthCare and GE Vernova, which are reported as discontinued operations in all periods presented) [DOC ge_fy2024_notes.txt]. On this consistent, apples-to-apples basis:

- FY2022 revenue (GE Aerospace continuing operations, as recast in the FY2024 10-K): **$29,139 million** [DOC ge_fy2024_income_statement.txt]
- FY2024 revenue (GE Aerospace): **$38,702 million** [DOC ge_fy2024_income_statement.txt]

Using these comparable, continuing-operations figures, revenue growth from FY2022 to FY2024 was:

($38,702M − $29,139M) / $29,139M ≈ 32.8%

ANSWER: Revenue grew approximately 32.8% (from $29,139 million in FY2022 to $38,702 million in FY2024), using GE Aerospace's continuing-operations basis as recast in its FY2024 10-K (which excludes the spun-off GE HealthCare and GE Vernova businesses). Note: this differs greatly from a comparison using GE's originally reported FY2022 total revenue of $76,555 million, which included the now-divested HealthCare and Vernova segments and is not a valid comparison to the current GE Aerospace entity.
